formula_checks.name: accountClassBreakdown
formula_checks.why: The linked-account reconciliation is elaborate and usually conserves the balance, but a hand-built account with an unpriced holding or negative/overdrawn balance can create allocation cases not fully specified. “Cash above zero, never more than balance” is ambiguous when balance is negative.
formula_checks.should_be: All returned class portions must sum to the account balance exactly; missing-priced holdings should absorb the residual only under the specified class rule, and impossible/negative cases need an explicit refusal or reconciliation rule.

formula_checks.name: classPortionLabel
formula_checks.why: The labels mostly match the class split, but “government” is treated as a Treasury synonym, broader than the owner-confirmed broker terms TREAS, UST, T-bill, T-note, T-bond. It can mislabel agency/government bonds as Treasuries.
formula_checks.should_be: Use only the approved Treasury tokens; otherwise label the holding as a bond unless a CD token is present.

formula_checks.name: assetAllocation
formula_checks.why: It says the seven class totals add to everything owned, but does not say how a missing balance or missing breakdown is exposed; a class split may be unknown rather than zero.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum each account’s known class portions and flag incomplete accounts; do not certify the total as complete while a balance is missing.

formula_checks.name: earmarkDefault
formula_checks.why: The default share depends on whether the caller supplies the household home/car identity. “Told nothing” makes a property with no use 0%, while the owner rule says the first property is the home when none is marked and no use is stated; those paths can disagree.
formula_checks.should_be: Always resolve home/car identity from the shared property-use and primary-vehicle rules before applying 0%/100% defaults; distinguish “not asked” from “none exists”.

formula_checks.name: primaryCarIdOf
formula_checks.why: Selects only accounts of kind vehicle, chooses largest balance and breaks ties by textual ID order. This follows DEC-2746b and avoids valuables being mistaken for the car.

formula_checks.name: earmarkedAmount
formula_checks.why: The formula says a saved share is held between 0% and 100% but does not state whether out-of-range inputs are clamped, rejected, or ignored.
formula_checks.should_be: Clamp only if that is the agreed input contract; otherwise validate/refuse invalid saved percentages. Never calculate a negative or over-100% earmark silently.

formula_checks.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
formula_checks.why: The total is the sum of earmarked amounts, but no handling is stated for accounts with missing balances. Missing values should not silently disappear from a complete-looking nest egg.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum known earmarked amounts and expose missing-value accounts/incompleteness.

formula_checks.name: benchmarkReturn
formula_checks.why: The 6% fallback for unknown/missing kind is explicit, and benchmarkInfo is specified to label a missing-record kind “Generic blended estimate” with estimate=true. The downstream label must be used.

formula_checks.name: blendedVolatility
formula_checks.why: A weighted average of individual volatilities is not generally the volatility of a combined portfolio unless the holdings move together. The formula acknowledges no covariance table exists, so calling it portfolio volatility overstates what it measures.
formula_checks.should_be: Label it as a weighted average of holding-level volatility estimates, or calculate portfolio volatility with correlations/covariances. Refuse when no amount is earmarked.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary portfolio-risk mathematics; card’s own caveat.

formula_checks.name: benchmarkInfo
formula_checks.why: It carries the rate from benchmarkReturn and labels custom rates as estimates, including zero; fallback generic rate is explicitly identified as an estimate.

formula_checks.name: blendedReturn
formula_checks.why: The benchmark rate is weighted by each account’s retirement-earmarked amount and refuses when that total is zero. This follows the stated nest-egg definition.

formula_checks.name: earmarkedKinds
formula_checks.why: It counts kinds among non-property accounts with positive earmark and substitutes “other” for no kind, but does not specify how a property held in a retirement account or invalid earmark is treated.
formula_checks.should_be: Use positive earmark and distinct normalized kind values; represent missing kind as other only as an explicit owner-approved fallback.

formula_checks.name: buildAssetsState
formula_checks.why: The formula explicitly defines shares as 0 when the total is 0 and refuses an average return. It is an exceptional undefined-total state, not an arithmetic claim that shares sum to 100 in that case.

formula_checks.name: assetsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: The formula creates “savings or portfolio” as taxable Stocks / Funds, which may misclassify a bank-savings answer as an investment. The source does not define whether that onboarding answer means cash savings or an investment portfolio.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the user’s selected meaning: savings account → Cash; portfolio/holdings → Stocks / Funds. Ask if the source answer conflates them.

formula_checks.name: monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: The 401(k) cap and match arithmetic are specified, but the formula needs boundary tests for age as attained in the current year, the 60–63 catch-up tier, and whether employer match percentage is applied to the capped employee contribution or compensation. It also mixes a 401(k) elective limit with a Roth answer of unknown account type by design.
formula_checks.should_be: Apply the published 2026 elective limit for age reached this year; cap employee 401(k) amount before computing percentage match as owner specifies; keep Roth amount as entered and exclude property savings.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-2746e and DEC-3035k; 2026 IRS elective-deferral limits as stated in the brief. IRS official 2026 limits: https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/retirement-topics-401k-and-profit-sharing-plan-contribution-limits

formula_checks.name: getAssetsState
formula_checks.why: It delegates to assetsStateFrom and returns nothing for absent/empty saved accounts, consistent with the no-accounts rule.

formula_checks.name: sourceWording
formula_checks.why: It distinguishes Linked, Imported and By hand; it does not invent an age when no sync is recorded and adds an age only from a successful sync at four or more days.

formula_checks.name: historyCoverage
formula_checks.why: The whole-month sentence logic is detailed, but the card does not specify what happens when the recorded history start is in the future or when the history start date is malformed. Also, “part month” uses days ÷ days in that month, but the sentence intentionally uses only whole months; test this split.
formula_checks.should_be: Validate dates; never produce negative coverage for a future start; round down the numeric month measure and build the sentence only from whole months.

formula_checks.name: uberGroupOf
formula_checks.why: The three-way mapping is explicit and consistent with the described Net worth grouping.

formula_checks.name: uberGroupRows
formula_checks.why: The grouping and sum rules are clear, but a missing balance or an account with no usable class split can make group totals look complete despite missing information.
formula_checks.should_be: Group the known class rows and totals, while propagating a missing-data indicator; for complete data the three groups must add to What you own.

formula_checks.name: itemizedTotal
formula_checks.why: It adds only entered values in exact decimals, leaves missing values out, and counts negative values; this is consistent with the stated purpose.

formula_checks.name: itemizeRemainder
formula_checks.why: Entered total minus exact sum of known itemized values is correct, including negative remainder when holdings exceed the entered amount.

formula_checks.name: itemizedResultTotal
formula_checks.why: The new total equals the entered total when itemized holdings do not exceed it and equals the holdings sum when they do, so itemizing cannot reduce the account total.

formula_checks.name: buildItemizedAccounts
formula_checks.why: The propagation rules are detailed and match owner decisions, but a listed holding with no value is still described as “balance = its value” without stating whether an account is created with missing balance or omitted. That affects total preservation and itemizeMissingCount.
formula_checks.should_be: Create each holding account while preserving a missing value as missing; carry the original wrapper/source/retirement share; never invent bond face value/rate; create residual cash only for positive known remainder.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-2746h and DEC-3035m; tenets 3 and 5.

formula_checks.name: correctClassOf
formula_checks.why: Name evidence is applied before maturity date, and it does not explicitly preserve a user-confirmed class. This conflicts with the owner’s rule that any maturity-dated instrument is Bonds & CDs and that confirmed classes are never overwritten; it can also infer from property names, contrary to DEC-3035o.
formula_checks.should_be: For unconfirmed accounts, apply maturity date before safe name evidence; exclude property names from name inference; preserve confirmed class.

formula_checks.name: reclassifyAccounts
formula_checks.why: Holding reclassification makes every non-cash name-evidenced holding without a bond name Stocks / Funds, and does not preserve a person-confirmed holding class or Unclassified when evidence is absent. This conflicts with DEC-2484r and DEC-3035f.
formula_checks.should_be: Do not overwrite a person-confirmed class; only correct when clear current evidence and the owner’s precedence rules establish a class; otherwise keep Unclassified and ask.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-2484r and DEC-3035f; tenets 3 and 5.

cases.formula_gives: Uses 2026 $35,750 annual limit / 12; match is applied to the capped contribution.

cases.name: historyCoverage
cases.title: 18 whole months plus part month is not rounded up
cases.given: History starts 2025-04-01; today 2026-10-09.

expected.wording: 1 year and 6 months of history, starting Apr 1, 2025

working: Apr 1, 2025 to Oct 1, 2026 = 18 whole months.
Oct 1 to Oct 9 is 8/31 = 0.258 months; numeric month coverage rounds down to one decimal, 18.2.
Oct 1 to Oct 9 is 8/31 = 0.258 months; numeric month coverage rounds to one decimal, 18.3.

cases.name: historyCoverage

expected.result: RULE UNCLEAR — should reject invalid future history start or report no history; formula does not specify negative coverage behavior

working: The start date is in the future.
Formula does not define this invalid record.
cases.notes: Future date validation is unspecified.
cases.formula_gives: Could produce a negative months-covered sentence; no future-date refusal stated.

cases.name: reclassifyAccounts
cases.title: Gold holding must become Alternatives, not Stocks / Funds
cases.given: An unconfirmed account contains a holding named Gold; it is currently filed as Stocks / Funds, with no user-confirmed holding class.
working: “Gold” is safe name evidence for Alternatives.
The formula says any non-bond class other than cash becomes Stocks / Funds, so it would leave/reassign this holding to Stocks / Funds instead of Alternatives.
The correct classification is Alternatives.
cases.notes: This case directly tests the formula’s overly broad “any other class ... a stock or fund” branch.
cases.formula_gives: Stocks / Funds (the formula’s fallback for name evidence other than bonds/cash)
